prerequisites: Computer and network knowledge from basic degree courses

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to design, develop, evaluate and ensure the accessibility, ergonomics, usability and security of computer systems, services and applications, as well as the information they manage.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, autonomy and creativity. Ability to communicate and transmit the knowledge, skills and abilities of the profession of Technical Engineer in Computer Science.
Knowledge, administration and maintenance of computer systems, services and applications.
Administration and maintenance of computer systems, services and applications.
Knowledge of computer systems, services and applications.
Knowledge of the services and management tools that integrate an operating system.
Perform basic administration tasks of a multi-tasking operating system in a network environment.
Install and configure applications and services in a computer system (physical or in the cloud), in order to achieve the required functionality for the system.

syllabus_topics: Installation, startup and exploitation of systems
Concepts of system administration. Installation of Linux and Windows operating systems. Linux administrative tools. Windows administration console.
System startup and shutdown. Startup sequence. Linux service startup and shutdown scripts: runlevels, upstart, systemd. Troubleshooting Linux and Windows startup problems.
Resource management and growth planning
Disks and file systems: ext3-4, NTFS. Journals. Disk administration. Partitioning. Logical volumes. Disk arrays. Partition managers. Quotas. Other storage devices.
Linux and Windows directory structure. Software installation and update. Linux packages. System update. Kernel modules. Windows drivers.
Backups. Backup tools. Simple backup. Multi-level backup.
User management and administration. Authentication systems
User accounts. Creation, deletion, change of local user properties.
Local user authentication. Local groups. Resource access permissions.
Network configuration and shared resources.
Network configuration of a computer
Network authentication (LDAP, Kerberos, Active Directory)
Windows Networks. Active Directory. Domains. Organizational Units.
IPv6 concepts
Basic services
Firewalls: iptables, firewalls in Windows.
Network file systems: NFS and Samba/CIFS. Network backup.
Windows and Linux network services (DNS, WINS, DHCP, mail, SSH, Terminal Server, etc.)
Server migrations and basic virtualization concepts
Migration of physical Linux servers
Migration of physical Windows servers
Virtualization solutions
Migration of a physical server to a virtual server
Installation of operating systems and database applications.
Resource design and exploitation
System recovery
User administration
Network configuration and basic services
Backups and scheduled tasks
Migration and virtualization
Installation and configuration of cloud systems

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of individual or group assignments related to theory
Formative and continuous evaluation in practical work
Final evaluation of practical work (product, report, oral presentation)
Theoretical exam (if average theory assignment score is below 7)

assessment_rules: The final grade calculation depends on the performance in theory assignments. If the average score in theory assignments is 7 or higher, the final grade is calculated as (0.5 × Practical work grade) + (0.5 × Average theory assignments). If the average score in theory assignments is below 7, a theoretical exam is required, and the final grade is calculated as (0.5 × Practical work grade) + (0.35 × Average theory assignments) + (0.15 × Theoretical exam grade). It is necessary to pass the theoretical and practical parts of the subject separately. The professor may require students to demonstrate knowledge in their submissions via videoconference.
